classifications.label: Systematic calibration drift or instrumental non-linearity affecting each apparatus differently
Environmental or operational cyclic forcing on a ~6–8 day timescale, decoupling the instruments
Measurement or transcription error correlated with apparatus or time, introducing spurious anti-correlations
True physical decoupling: the four measurement streams are responding to genuinely different aspects of the system, not a single shared measurand
Insufficient data: 10 days and 60–102 trials per stream are below the threshold to establish true baseline correlations; apparent patterns are statistical artifacts of limited sample size
Genuine environmental or thermal transient on day 15 affecting resonator_lab specifically
Measurement or recording error introduced on day 15 in resonator_lab data acquisition or calibration
True short-timescale instrumental instability in resonator_lab (e.g., frequency servo drift, optical cavity mode-hop, or mechanical resonance shift) triggered on day 15
Insufficient baseline data (only 84 trials over 10 days) means the day 15 cluster is within normal variance, and the apparent bimodal structure is a statistical artifact of small-n sampling
Operator or procedural change on day 15 (e.g., different person, different measurement protocol, different sampling rate or averaging window) affecting resonator_lab data quality
Cross-instrument correlations are noise artifacts; instruments are genuinely independent but underpowered to detect their mutual influence
Environmental or electromagnetic forcing couples all four instruments via a shared external driver, with instrument-specific time lags reflecting different thermal or mechanical response times

Low-level measurement or calibration error common to the entire ensemble (e.g., clock drift, systematic digital quantization, common reference offset) creates spurious cross-correlations masking true instrument independence

Instruments are independent and measurements valid, but the ensemble is too small (n~150–314 trials each) and correlations too weak to generate publishable conclusions; continue baseline until effect sizes stabilize or anomalies emerge

One or more instruments has a latent hardware fault (aging component, creeping misalignment, or intermittent electrical contact) that manifests as anomalous coupling or autocorrelation structure on intermediate timescales (days 5–15)

Pendulum_lab and resonator_obs data streams are aliased or systematically offset copies of each other, indicating a data entry, labeling, or software synchronization error rather than genuine instrument independence.

The r=1.000 pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation is a statistical artifact: I have searched across many time lags and offsets, and by chance alone, one of these searches will produce an extremely high value; this is the one.

Pendulum_lab and resonator_obs measure the same underlying physical quantity (e.g., environmental oscillation or mechanical resonance) via different physical transducers, and the 3-day offset reflects a real phase lag in the settlement's environment or apparatus coupling.

Measurement ensemble is currently too immature to distinguish artifact from signal; continue to ~n=600–1000 trials per instrument, recompute all correlations, and re-evaluate only when the pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs r=1.000 finding is either independently replicated in a fresh batch or disappears with extended sampling.

Residual (undiscovered mechanism): a flaw in my hypothesis-generation process, in the experimental design, or in my understanding of the settlement's environment or instrumentation that I have not yet considered.

Day 36 pendulum_lab excursion is genuine environmental or instrumental transient (thermal, mechanical, or settlement-wide vibration spike on Day 36 only); other instruments insensitive or damped to this transient.

pendulum_lab underwent recalibration, environmental isolation failure, or instrument drift onset between trials 234 (Day 35) and 235 (Day 36); the excursion marks the start of instrument degradation or a step-change in systematic error.

pendulum_lab Day 36 excursion is a data entry or trial-assignment error: the six readings (trials 235–240) were mislabeled or incorrectly linked to the wrong date/instrument, introducing artificial variance.

The r=1.000 pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation (from prior review) is a data integrity anomaly that invalidates cross-instrument inference; Day 36 excursion is a secondary symptom of the same underlying record-keeping or software problem.

Day 36 pendulum_lab excursion is consistent with normal stochastic variation; the apparent mean shift is a random fluctuation within the post-baseline distribution and does not signal instrument or environmental change.

A mechanism or event outside my current awareness (e.g., a known operational or environmental protocol on Day 36, a colleague's test run, a partial instrument replacement, or a settlement event I did not log) explains the Day 36 pendulum_lab excursion.

pendulum_lab and resonator_obs data streams are aliased or mislabeled copies—pendulum_lab does not represent the instrument I believe it does, but rather a duplicate or relabeled feed from resonator_obs or an undocumented third source.

Day 36 pendulum_lab excursion (trials 235–240, mean 1.6704 vs. post-baseline 1.6656) is a genuine environmental or mechanical transient localized to the pendulum_lab apparatus, while other instruments remained stable because they are in a different physical location or have better vibration isolation.
pendulum_lab underwent unlogged recalibration, maintenance, or instrumental drift onset between Day 35 and Day 36; the excursion marks a step-change or the beginning of sustained degradation.

Data entry, trial-assignment, or instrument-labeling error introduced the Day 36 pendulum_lab anomaly: trials 235–240 were incorrectly linked to pendulum_lab and/or Day 36, when they actually belong to a different instrument or date.

An operational, maintenance, or environmental event on Day 36 that I did not log (colleague diagnostic test, settlement stress test, scheduled facility work) directly affected pendulum_lab or other instruments, and I was not informed or failed to record it.
